assessments.reasoning: GNU 1.3 [3605,5049) defines Transparent and Opaque copies and illustrates how the same format can serve different uses. [8127,8910) supplies the quantity threshold, the two per-copy alternatives, the public download conditions and the edition-specific duration.

challenge.method: Tested one Transparent copy for an entire multi-copy shipment with no per-copy location, a location restricted to private recipients, and removal one year after first distribution despite later retail distribution. Compared the corresponding paragraphs in all three editions.
challenge.results: A shipment-level copy alone fails the per-copy condition. A private location fails the general-public access condition. Measuring from first distribution can cut the access period short when the edition is distributed again. Exactly 100 misses the threshold. At 101 Opaque copies the work’s Cover Text designation is immaterial. Versions 1.2 and 1.3 retain public download and public-standard protocols. Version 1.1 supplies additional express language about anonymity and price that cannot simply be imported into 1.3. In 1.3 the qualification about added material describes the contents of the download.

limitations: Transparency depends on the §1 criteria for editing and processing the actual representation. A filename suffix cannot settle it. Reasonable prudence and the last qualifying distribution date are factual.
Version 1.3 does not expressly repeat 1.1’s anonymous-download and zero-charge terms. Whether a particular access arrangement affords the required public access remains fact-dependent.
reasoning: GNU 1.3 §3 applies upon publication or distribution of more than 100 Opaque copies. Each must carry a machine-readable Transparent copy or state, in or with that Opaque copy, where the general network-using public can download the complete Transparent document without added material using public-standard protocols. On the network route, reasonably prudent steps begin when distribution in quantity starts. They must address access at the stated location through at least one year after the distributor’s last public distribution of an Opaque copy of that edition, including through agents or retailers.
